cases.sentence: Он мог бы чувства обнаружить, а не щетиниться, как ___.
cases.translation: He could have shown his feelings, not bristled like a beast
cases.explain: Зверь stands in the nominative because как (like) equates it to the subject он in the same case.

cases.translation: Beds are made up for the guests
cases.explain: The preposition для (for) always governs the genitive case, so гости becomes гостей.

cases.sentence: Он, правда, в туз из ___ в пяти сажениях попадал.
cases.translation: True, he could hit an ace with a pistol from five fathoms away
cases.explain: The preposition из (out of/with) governs the genitive case, so пистолет becomes пистолета.

cases.sentence: Онегин с первого движения к ___ такого поручения сказал, что он всегда готов.
cases.translation: From his first reaction to the messenger of such a commission, Onegin said he was always ready
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) always requires the dative case, so посол becomes послу.

cases.sentence: И ___ достался в плен дорогой залог.
cases.translation: And a costly pledge fell captive to the French
cases.explain: The verb достался (fell to/became the property of) governs the dative of the recipient, so французы becomes французам.

cases.translation: Having arrived home, he inspected the pistols
cases.explain: Пистолеты is the plural direct object of the transitive verb осмотрел (inspected), so it takes the accusative.

cases.translation: He carries home the terrible treasure (the body)
cases.explain: Клад is the direct object of the transitive verb везет (carries), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Кипя ___ нетерпеливой, ответа дома ждет поэт.
cases.translation: Boiling with impatient hostility, the poet awaits an answer at home
cases.explain: The gerund кипя (boiling/seething) takes an instrumental of the emotion one is filled with, so вражда becomes враждой.

cases.sentence: В философической ___ Зарецкий, некогда Буян, живет и здравствует.
cases.translation: In philosophical solitude, Zaretsky, once a brawler, lives on in good health
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating static location requires the prepositional case, so пустыня becomes пустыне.

reading.ru: Заметив, что Владимир скрылся, Онегин с кукой угоним.
reading.question: What does Onegin do after noticing Vladimir has left the party?
options: He sinks into thought near Olga
reading.correct: He sinks into thought near Olga
reading.explain: The text says that noticing Vladimir gone, Onegin, near Olga, sank into thought, pleased with himself.

reading.ru: Но кончен он, идут за ужин, постели стелют для гостей.
reading.question: What happens once the cotillion (dance) is over?
options: Everyone goes to supper, then beds are made up for the guests
reading.correct: Everyone goes to supper, then beds are made up for the guests
reading.explain: The text says once the dance ended, they went to supper, and beds were prepared for the guests staying over.

reading.ru: Татьяна бедная не спит и в поле темное глядит.
reading.question: What does poor Tatiana do while everyone else sleeps?
options: She stays awake, gazing into the dark field
She sleeps more soundly than ever
reading.correct: She stays awake, gazing into the dark field
reading.explain: The text says 'poor Tatiana does not sleep, and gazes into the dark field,' troubled by Onegin's behavior.

reading.ru: Погибнут, Аня говорит. Но гибель от него любезна.
reading.question: What does Tatiana say she fears will happen, involving Onegin and Lensky?
options: That they will perish, but even ruin from him would be dear to her
That they will become inseparable friends again
That Lensky will forgive Onegin instantly
That nothing serious will come of it
reading.correct: That they will perish, but even ruin from him would be dear to her
reading.explain: Tatiana says 'they will perish,' yet admits that even destruction coming from Onegin would be dear to her.

reading.ru: В пяти верстах от Красногорья деревни Ленского живет.
reading.question: How far from Lensky's village does Zaretsky live?
options: In the same house as Lensky
reading.correct: Five versts away, near Krasnogorye
reading.explain: The text places Zaretsky's home 'five versts from Krasnogorye,' near Lensky's village.

reading.ru: Зарецкий, некогда Буян, Картерной шайки Атаман.
reading.question: What was Zaretsky's reputation in his younger days?
options: A brawler and ataman (chief) of a gambling gang
reading.correct: A brawler and ataman (chief) of a gambling gang
reading.explain: The text describes Zaretsky as once 'a brawler, ataman of a card-sharping gang.'

reading.ru: Он, правда, в туз из пистолета в пяти сажениях попадал.
reading.question: What skill of Zaretsky's is mentioned regarding pistols?
options: He could hit an ace at five fathoms with a pistol
He had never fired a pistol in his life
He only used swords, never pistols
reading.correct: He could hit an ace at five fathoms with a pistol
reading.explain: The text says he truly 'could hit an ace with a pistol at five sazhens.'

reading.ru: И французам достался в плен дорогой залог.
reading.question: What happened to Zaretsky during a military campaign, according to the text?
options: He fell into French captivity as a valuable prisoner
reading.correct: He fell into French captivity as a valuable prisoner
reading.explain: The text says he fell drunk from his horse and 'a costly pledge fell captive to the French.'

reading.ru: Он был не глуп.
reading.question: How does the narrator ultimately assess Zaretsky's intelligence, despite his rough reputation?
reading.correct: He was not stupid
reading.explain: Despite his checkered past, the narrator states plainly, 'he was not stupid.'

reading.ru: То был приятный, благородный, Короткий вызов, иль картель.
reading.question: What does Zaretsky deliver to Onegin from Lensky?
options: A polite, noble, brief challenge to a duel
A love letter meant for Olga
reading.correct: A polite, noble, brief challenge to a duel
reading.explain: The text describes the note as 'a pleasant, noble, brief challenge, or cartel' — a formal duel challenge.

reading.ru: Онегин с первого движения к послу такого поручения, обратясь, без лишних слов сказал, что он всегда готов.
reading.question: How does Onegin respond to receiving the duel challenge via Zaretsky?
options: Immediately and without extra words, he says he is always ready
He refuses to answer at all
He laughs it off as a joke
He asks for several days to consider
reading.correct: Immediately and without extra words, he says he is always ready
reading.explain: The text says Onegin, from his very first reaction, said without extra words that he was always ready (for the duel).

reading.ru: Он обвинял себя во многом.
reading.question: How does Onegin feel about his own conduct, once alone after agreeing to the duel?
options: He blames himself for many things
He feels completely justified and proud
reading.correct: He blames himself for many things
reading.explain: Alone with his conscience, the text says 'he accused himself of much,' regretting his earlier flirtation with Olga.

reading.ru: Кипя враждой нетерпеливой, ответа дома ждет поэт.
reading.question: How does Lensky wait at home for Onegin's reply?
reading.correct: Seething with impatient hostility
reading.explain: The text describes Lensky 'boiling with impatient hostility' as he awaits the reply at home.

reading.ru: Прыгнула Оленька с крыльца, подобно ветреной надежде.
reading.question: How does Olga greet Lensky when he visits her before the duel, unaware of his intentions?
options: She bounds off the porch to greet him, like a fickle hope
She refuses to see him at all
She bursts into tears at the sight of him
reading.correct: She bounds off the porch to greet him, like a fickle hope
reading.explain: The text describes Olga leaping from the porch 'like a fickle hope,' happy and carefree, unaware of the coming duel.

reading.ru: Он смотрит сладком умиленье, Он видит, он еще любим.
reading.question: How does Lensky feel after seeing Olga's affectionate, innocent behavior?
options: He is sweetly moved, seeing that he is still loved
He becomes angrier and more jealous
He decides to cancel the duel on the spot
He feels nothing has changed his resolve
reading.correct: He is sweetly moved, seeing that he is still loved
reading.explain: The text says he looks on with sweet tenderness, seeing 'he is still loved,' and his jealousy nearly melts away.

reading.ru: Домой приехав пистолеты, он осмотрел.
reading.question: What does Onegin do with the pistols once he arrives back home?
options: He hides them from his servant
reading.correct: He inspects them
reading.explain: The text says 'having come home, he inspected the pistols,' preparing methodically for the duel.

reading.ru: Куда, куда вы удалились весны моей золотые дни?
reading.question: What question does Lensky pose in the verses he writes the night before the duel?
options: Where have the golden days of my spring departed to?
What is the meaning of true friendship?
reading.correct: Where have the golden days of my spring departed to?
reading.explain: Lensky's poem begins, 'Where, where have you fled, golden days of my spring?' — a meditation on his fleeting youth.

reading.ru: Но ошибался он. Евгений спал в это время мертвым сном.
reading.question: What is ironic about Zaretsky's assumption that Onegin would already be awake and ready?
options: Onegin was actually sleeping like the dead at that hour
Onegin had already left for the duel site alone
Onegin was awake writing his own poem
Onegin had canceled the duel overnight
reading.correct: Onegin was actually sleeping like the dead at that hour
reading.explain: The text says Zaretsky was mistaken: 'Evgeny slept at this time a dead sleep,' oversleeping on the morning of the duel.

reading.ru: Спешит Онегин одеваться, слуге велит приготовляться.
reading.question: What does Onegin do once he finally wakes up and realizes the time?
options: He rushes to get dressed and orders his servant to prepare
He decides to skip the duel entirely
He writes a farewell letter first
reading.correct: He rushes to get dressed and orders his servant to prepare
reading.explain: Realizing he is late, 'Onegin hurries to dress, orders his servant to get ready' for the duel.

reading.ru: Идет Онегин с извинением.
reading.question: How does Onegin approach Zaretsky and Lensky upon his late arrival at the dueling ground?
options: With an apology, since he is late
In complete silence, refusing to speak
reading.correct: With an apology, since he is late
reading.explain: The text says 'Onegin approaches with an apology' for his tardiness.

reading.ru: Зарецкий губу закусил.
reading.question: How does Zaretsky react when Onegin names his valet Guillot as his second?
options: He bites his lip in disapproval
He refuses to continue the duel
reading.correct: He bites his lip in disapproval
reading.explain: Displeased that Onegin's second is merely his valet, Zaretsky 'bit his lip' in silent disapproval.

reading.ru: Вот пистолеты уж блеснули.
reading.question: What signals that the duel is about to begin?
options: The pistols have already gleamed/flashed into view
A church bell rings in the distance
reading.correct: The pistols have already gleamed/flashed into view
reading.explain: The text says 'now the pistols have already gleamed,' as the duel formally begins.

reading.ru: Но как раз Онегин выстрелил.
reading.question: What happens just as Lensky begins to take aim?
options: Both men fire at the same instant
reading.correct: Onegin fires first
reading.explain: The text says that just as Lensky was taking aim, 'Onegin fired' first, fatally.

reading.ru: Молодой певец нашел безвременный конец.
reading.question: What is the fate of Lensky, the young poet, after the shot?
options: He survives with only a minor wound
He forgives Onegin before dying peacefully of old age later
reading.correct: He meets an untimely end (death)
reading.explain: The text states starkly that 'the young singer found an untimely end,' confirming Lensky's death.

reading.ru: Домой везет он страшный клад.
reading.question: What does Zaretsky do with Lensky's body after the duel?
options: He carries the terrible burden (the corpse) home on a sledge
He buries it at the dueling site immediately
He leaves it for the villagers to find
He takes it to Onegin's house
reading.correct: He carries the terrible burden (the corpse) home on a sledge
reading.explain: The text says Zaretsky lays the frozen corpse on the sledge and 'carries the terrible treasure home.'

highlight.question: Which two lines contrast where the guests slept with where Onegin went?
highlight.explain: Line 1 describes the guests being given lodging in the house, while line 4 shows that Onegin alone rode home to sleep.

highlight.question: Which two lines describe Onegin's range of conversational abilities?
highlight.explain: Line 2 shows his skill in arguing cheerfully, while line 4 demonstrates his ability to remain silent when calculated to do so.

highlight.question: Which two lines show the poet waiting for a response from Onegin and receiving it?
highlight.explain: Line 1 shows Lensky waiting at home for an answer, and line 3 reveals that the neighbor has brought Onegin's formal response.

highlight.question: Which two lines show Lensky's emotional turmoil as he prepared to leave Olga?
sentences: Шептал: не правда ль? я счастлив.
highlight.explain: Line 2 indicates it is time to leave and his heart is constricted, while line 3 emphasizes his heart was full of sorrow.

highlight.question: Which two lines describe the French servant preparing Onegin's clothing?
highlight.explain: Line 2 shows the servant offering a robe and slippers, while line 3 indicates he provides linen for Onegin to wear.

highlight.question: Which two lines show both duelists taking their positions to fire?
sentences: Стал также целить — но как раз
highlight.explain: Line 1 shows the first person quietly raising his pistol, and line 3 shows Lensky squinting his eye as he also begins to aim.
